title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
A Tesla vehicle using Autopilot was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family of the deceased that data from the vehicle recording what happened was unavailable. A hacker later demonstrated that such data is retained on every Tesla vehicle, contradicting the company's assertion to the family.

This is a failure of transparency in a safety-critical deployment. The system operated without adequate human verification of factual claims made about its data retention. The failure occurred in Tesla's response to a crash, not in the Autopilot system itself, but in the company's handling of evidence about how the system performed.

A jury found Tesla liable and ordered it to pay damages. What is not established is whether Tesla's initial claim about missing data reflected a genuine misunderstanding of the vehicle's capabilities or a knowing misrepresentation.
